title: Pastels, Fried Fish Pies
author: SAVEUR (May 2012 print issue; page credits photographer Penny De Los Santos)
desc: An egg-and-oil dough rolled to an eighth of an inch, cut into three-inch rounds, filled with white fish, parsley, basil, cilantro and habanero, and fried at 350°.
longDesc: The Saveur printing makes about two dozen pies. A shaggy dough of flour, one egg and six tablespoons of water is kneaded about six minutes and rested an hour. Garlic, onion and a minced habanero are cooked about five minutes, then mixed with eight ounces of white fish — mackerel, trout or dorado — and chopped parsley, cilantro and basil. Rounds are cut with a three-inch cutter, a teaspoon of filling goes in each, and the pies are folded to half-moons, crimped with a fork and fried in two inches of oil. Note that the raw fish is cooked only by the six-minute fry.
ingredients: 2 tbsp canola oil, plus oil for frying (frying quantity: oil to a depth of 2 inches)
6 tbsp water — appears only in the method
1 habanero or Scotch bonnet chile, stemmed, seeded, minced
8 oz white fish, such as mackerel, trout or dorado
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper — quantities not printed
steps: Stir the flour, egg and 6 tablespoons of water until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a work surface about 6 minutes, until smooth. Wrap in plastic and rest 1 hour.

Heat the 2 tablespoons of oil in a 2-quart saucepan over medium-high. Cook the garlic, onion and chile, stirring, about 5 minutes, until soft. Transfer to a bowl and stir in the fish, parsley, cilantro, basil, salt and pepper.

Roll the dough to an 1/8-inch-thick circle. Cut about 24 rounds with a 3-inch cutter. Put about 1 teaspoon of filling in the centre of each, wet half of the edge, fold into a half-moon, press to seal and crimp with a fork.

Pour oil to a depth of 2 inches into a 6-quart Dutch oven and heat over medium-high until a deep-fry thermometer reads 350° (unit not printed). Fry in batches about 6 minutes, until golden brown and the filling is cooked through. Drain on parchment and serve hot with kaani sauce.
chefTips: The printed cue is ‘golden brown and the filling is cooked through’ — the fish goes in uncooked, so do not pull the pies early.
Fry in batches so the oil does not drop in temperature.
The page does not include a kaani sauce; use SEN090.
commonMistakes: Overfilling: a teaspoon is what the page prints.
Letting the fish be fully raw in a too-brief fry.
Skipping the fork crimp and losing filling in the oil.
storage: Fry the day you eat them; keeps 1 day refrigerated.
reheating: Recrisp in a hot oven 8 to 10 minutes.
healthBenefits: White fish is a lean protein.
Fresh herbs and chile add flavour without added sugar.
culturalNote: SAVEUR’s May 2012 Senegal feature was written by John O’Connor (‘A Feast for All’); the recipes themselves carry no personal byline. This one first appeared in the May 2012 issue and was republished online on 30 September 2013.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Pastels (Fried Fish Pies)’. Byline status: magazine, no individual author; the page credits Penny De Los Santos, and does not say whether she wrote the recipe or shot it — treated as a photo credit. Publication: SAVEUR, online 30 September 2013, first in the May 2012 issue. Yield ‘about 2 dozen’; the ‘Serves’ value is absent. SINGLE-PASS.
Printed temperatures: 350° (unit not printed). Printed doneness cues, in fragments: ‘until a shaggy dough forms’; ‘until smooth’; ‘until soft’; ‘until golden brown and the filling is cooked through’.
ABSENT, not estimated: salt and pepper amounts, the page’s own kaani sauce (none included). The page lists 6 tbsp water only in the method.
UNRECONCILED with SEN067: different dough (this one has an egg and oil).
